construct: a div-built table whose HEADER row differs from the body rows by weight (700) and fill - no table formatting context involved
why: The one property that makes a table read as a table. Built out of flex rows on purpose, so it measures the header/body DISTINCTION rather than dying on the `display: table` wall the semantic case pins. If this fails, no data table is drawable by any route; if it passes, the div-table is a viable shape and the semantic-markup refusal is a spelling problem rather than an archetype problem.

canvas.note: the header row is a frame with its own fill and a bolder text style

mustHave: the table header row is visually distinct from the body rows
the header row's text is bolder than the body rows' text
the header row has a different background fill from the body rows
the header row sits above both body rows
